method: Actual source images opened with view_image and read. Printed/PDF pages use selected registry editions; PDF positions one-based.

records.observed: Cook separates two independent stem tenses from periphrastic tense labels. Present can express future, preterite any of three past-tense senses. Passive uses wesan/bēon or weorðan with past participle. His schematic English comparison must be qualified by contextual evidence.
Habban plus past participle is specified for transitives and wesan for intransitives. Finite agreement is with the subject. Does not establish an invariant English-to-OE auxiliary substitution.
Willan primarily expresses wish/intention. A simple present can express future. Keep selected course forms; Fulk stress marks are not imported.

Habban plus past participle resembles a perfect; simple preterites can also translate present/past perfect. Intransitives more commonly use bēon/weorðan. Ær can mark anteriority. Present-participle periphrases may be durative; simple forms may receive progressive English translations.
Context licenses several English tense/aspect renderings of one simple tense. Bēon forms also have habitual/gnomic use, despite the table’s future label; no automatic future translation.
Nabban indicative is already recognition. Sęcgan present/preterite/subjunctive alternatives are directly printed; actual course selections remain prior rather than silently changing.
Preterite-present inventory lists āgan and distinguishes whole lexical systems. Witan/nytan evidence is not a license to construct arbitrary unrecorded negatives.

Āgan: singular āh/āhst/āh, plural āgon, preterite āhte; nāgan is explicitly the negative companion. Infinitive/subjunctive/imperative/participle listings do not themselves assign all those systems in Unit12.

Wesan preterite and willan present/preterite with negative forms and optatives directly printed. Reported wolde remains intention where context requires it; not a general future-in-past transformation.

Accusative direct object and infinitival actor distinguished; §170 directly supports extent of time/space, using the storm all-day example. Measurement syntax requires its own evidence and is not inferred solely from this general duration rule.

Subjunctive may occur in independent and subordinate clauses. Keep ordinary content clauses separate from adverbial purpose/result; prior definitions do not automatically establish every new reported tense relation.

limits: These source observations guide reconciliation. Complete actual proposed cells, task dependencies and reading tokens still require individual review; no acceptance is inferred from a source citation alone.
